title: Overlay accuracy at angstrom-scale nodes
bottleneck: Patterning at 2nm and below requires aligning dozens of exposures with overlay errors below a nanometer, across wafers that warp and expand thermally. High-NA EUV's reduced depth of focus makes the process hypersensitive to focus and overlay drift, and chiplet/3D flows multiply the number of aligned layers. Current metrology samples only a fraction of fields, so drift can go undetected until wafers are scrapped.
why_it_blocks: Every overlay miss degrades transistor performance or kills dies outright; at these scales, misalignment is indistinguishable from a broken process. Yield learning stalls because the feedback loop between exposure and metrology is too slow and too sparse.
current_state: Advanced overlay control with in-situ metrology and machine-learning corrections is deployed at 3nm-class nodes, and ASML's latest scanners ship tighter overlay specs. Sub-nanometer control at HVM speeds is still aspirational.
